lines: One dead star spins 716 times a second.
Its equator moves at about 24% of light speed.
It's a neutron star under 16 kilometres in radius.
It sits about 18,000 light-years away, in Terzan 5.
Earth spinning that fast would fly apart instantly.
Only a neutron star's gravity can hold such spin together.
So the fastest spinners in the universe are also the densest.

evidence.claim: PSR J1748−2446ad is the fastest-spinning pulsar known, at 716.35 Hz (times per second), or 42,981 revolutions per minute.
If the neutron star is assumed to contain less than two times the mass of the Sun, its radius is constrained to be less than 16 km.
